question: A bruit audible over the thyroid gland is a finding specific to Graves disease and is NOT expected in toxic multinodular goitre, because the bruit in Graves disease results from increased vascularity of the entire gland driven by TSH-receptor antibody stimulation.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The thyroid bruit is a hallmark of Graves disease because TSH-receptor antibodies cause diffuse glandular hyperstimulation and increased vascularity. Toxic multinodular goitre does not produce a bruit as there is no diffuse antibody-driven stimulation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. A thyroid bruit (due to high vascularity from diffuse TSH-R Ab stimulation) is characteristic of Graves disease. In toxic multinodular goitre, vascularity is focal rather than diffuse, so a bruit is not typically present. Eye signs (exophthalmos, lid lag, lid retraction) similarly point to Graves disease.
